pharm-gp:enzyme.q: On a Lineweaver–Burk plot, a noncompetitive inhibitor:
o: Parallel line shift (both Vmax and Km ↓)

pharm-gp:enzyme.q: A 55-year-old man with recurrent gout starts a drug that is a structural analog of hypoxanthine and competes with it at the active site of xanthine oxidase. In vitro, adding excess hypoxanthine restores the maximal reaction rate. Which change in enzyme kinetics does the drug produce?
pharm-gp:enzyme.e: A competitive inhibitor raises apparent Km but is overcome by substrate, so Vmax is unchanged; a noncompetitive inhibitor lowers Vmax instead.

pharm-gp:pk.q: Steady state is reached after about:
pharm-gp:pk.e: Independent of dose for first-order drugs.

pharm-gp:pk.q: A 70-kg man with gram-negative sepsis must reach a target plasma concentration of 2 mg/L immediately with an IV antibiotic. The drug has a volume of distribution of 0.5 L/kg and a clearance of 5 L/h. What loading dose is required?
pharm-gp:pk.e: Loading dose = Vd × Cp / F = 35 L × 2 mg/L = 70 mg; 10 mg/h (CL × Cp) is the maintenance infusion rate, not the loading dose.

pharm-gp:metab.e: Constant amount eliminated per unit time.

pharm-gp:metab.q: A 62-year-old woman started hydralazine for hypertension 4 months ago. She now has arthralgia, a malar rash and pleuritic chest pain, and anti-histone antibodies are positive. Reduced activity of which drug-metabolizing pathway most increased her risk?
pharm-gp:metab.e: Drug-induced lupus from hydralazine, procainamide and isoniazid is more common in slow acetylators (phase II N-acetylation); glucuronidation is not the relevant pathway.

pharm-gp:pd.q: A drug with higher potency has:
In a trial, drugs A and B both lower systolic BP by a maximum of 30 mm Hg. Drug A produces half of this maximal effect at 5 mg, whereas drug B requires 50 mg. Which statement is correct?
o: A is more potent; efficacy is equal
B is more potent; efficacy is equal
A is more efficacious; potency is equal
A has the larger therapeutic index
pharm-gp:pd.e: Same Emax means equal efficacy; the lower EC₅₀ of drug A means greater potency. Therapeutic index cannot be judged without toxicity data.

pharm-gp:ansmap.q: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers to sweat glands release:

pharm-gp:ansmap.e: α₁ is Gq, α₂ is Gi, M₂ is Gi.

pharm-gp:ansmap.q: A 30-year-old man with primary palmar hyperhidrosis improves markedly with oral glycopyrrolate. Which description of the innervation of his eccrine sweat glands explains this response?
o: Parasympathetic fibers releasing ACh at M₃
Somatic motor fibers releasing ACh at Nₘ
Sympathetic fibers releasing ACh at M₃
Sympathetic fibers releasing NE at α₁
pharm-gp:ansmap.e: Eccrine sweat glands are sympathetic but cholinergic (muscarinic), so antimuscarinics reduce sweating; they have no parasympathetic supply.

pharm-gp:cholino.q: A 28-year-old woman has drooping eyelids and double vision that worsen toward evening and improve after rest. Repetitive nerve stimulation shows a decremental response, and anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies are positive. Which drug is most appropriate for symptom control?
pharm-gp:cholino.e: Myasthenia gravis is treated symptomatically with pyridostigmine, a peripheral AChE inhibitor that does not cross the BBB; bethanechol acts only at muscarinic receptors.

pharm-gp:antimusc.e: Hot as a hare, dry as a bone…
Scopolamine is used for motion sickness.

pharm-gp:antimusc.q: A 74-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia is started on a new drug for urge incontinence. Two days later he cannot void and has dry mouth, constipation and new confusion. Which drug action most likely caused these findings?
pharm-gp:antimusc.e: Antimuscarinics such as oxybutynin cause retention, dryness and delirium in older adults; β₃ agonists (mirabegron) treat overactive bladder without anticholinergic effects.

pharm-gp:symp.e: Used in cardiogenic shock and stress testing.

pharm-gp:symp.q: A 22-year-old woman develops hives, wheezing and BP 70/40 mm Hg minutes after eating peanuts. She receives intramuscular epinephrine and her BP rises to 110/70 mm Hg. Which receptor action most directly reversed her hypotension?
pharm-gp:symp.e: In anaphylaxis, epinephrine's α₁ vasoconstriction restores vascular tone while β₂ action relieves bronchospasm; β₂ vasodilation would lower BP.

pharm-gp:sympatholytic.e: Rebound hypertension if stopped abruptly. Central α₂ stimulation → ↓ sympathetic outflow.

pharm-gp:sympatholytic.q: First-dose orthostatic hypotension is typical of:

A 50-year-old man with resistant hypertension ran out of one of his medications 2 days ago. He now has headache, sweating, tremor and BP 210/115 mm Hg. The missing drug also caused dry mouth and sedation. What is the mechanism of his current BP rise?
o: Loss of central α₂ inhibition of sympathetic outflow
Rebound renin release after ACE inhibition is stopped
Unopposed α₁ effect after peripheral α₁ blockade ends
Upregulated β₁ receptors after β-blockade is withdrawn
pharm-gp:sympatholytic.e: Abrupt clonidine withdrawal removes central α₂-mediated sympathetic suppression, causing rebound hypertension; β-blocker withdrawal causes rebound tachycardia but without the prior sedation and dry mouth.

pharm-gp:bblock.q: A β-blocker with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity:

o: β₁ and β₂ but not α₁

pharm-gp:bblock.q: A 29-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has BP 165/110 mm Hg on repeated readings and no proteinuria. Which mechanism best describes the most appropriate oral antihypertensive?
o: Blocks α₁, β₁ and β₂ receptors
pharm-gp:bblock.e: Labetalol (mixed α₁/β blocker) is first-line in pregnancy; ACE inhibitors, ARBs and aliskiren are contraindicated because they cause fetal renal toxicity.

pharm-gp:pdei.e: Used for ED and pulmonary hypertension.

pharm-gp:pdei.q: Milrinone is a PDE3 inhibitor used for:
pharm-gp:pdei.e: ↑ cAMP → inotropy and vasodilation; cilostazol is PDE3 for claudication.

pharm-gp:pdei.q: A 58-year-old man with stable angina who takes isosorbide mononitrate daily asks for treatment of erectile dysfunction. Combining his nitrate with a PDE5 inhibitor would carry what major risk?
o: QT prolongation from K⁺ channel block
pharm-gp:pdei.e: Nitrates raise cGMP by NO release and PDE5 inhibitors prevent its breakdown, so together they cause profound vasodilation and hypotension.

pharm-tox:cardio.q: Which drug causes dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy?
Diffuse flushing during a rapid vancomycin infusion is due to:
pharm-tox:cardio.e: Slow the infusion and give antihistamines.

pharm-tox:cardio.q: A 58-year-old woman treated for breast cancer 2 years ago now has progressive exertional dyspnea. Echocardiography shows a dilated left ventricle with LVEF 30%; her regimen included a cumulative-dose-limited anthracycline. The mechanism of her cardiomyopathy is:
pharm-tox:cardio.e: Doxorubicin causes dose-dependent, largely irreversible cardiomyopathy via free radicals; trastuzumab (anti-HER2) causes reversible dysfunction.

pharm-tox:endorx.q: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is a classic adverse effect of:
Hyperprolactinemia with galactorrhea is most likely from:
pharm-tox:endorx.e: D₂ blockade removes dopamine's inhibition of prolactin.

pharm-tox:endorx.q: A 45-year-old man with bipolar disorder, stable on lithium for 10 years, has fatigue, weight gain, constipation and cold intolerance. TSH is 14 mU/L with a low free T₄; he takes no other drugs. Which action of lithium best explains these findings?
pharm-tox:endorx.e: Lithium is concentrated by the thyroid and inhibits release of T₄/T₃ (and iodine organification), causing hypothyroidism and goiter. Deiodinase inhibition (amiodarone, propranolol, PTU) lowers T₃, and enzyme induction matters mainly in patients already on levothyroxine.

pharm-tox:girx.e: Also NSAIDs. Take with a full glass of water and stay upright.

pharm-tox:girx.q: Which drug pair is classically linked to pancreatitis?
pharm-tox:girx.e: Also azathioprine, glucocorticoids and some diuretics.

pharm-tox:girx.q: A 30-year-old woman taking doxycycline for acne swallows her dose at bedtime with a sip of water and lies down. Two days later she has severe pain on swallowing; endoscopy shows a single discrete ulcer in the mid-esophagus with normal surrounding mucosa. Most likely diagnosis:
pharm-tox:girx.e: Tablets lodged near the aortic arch cause local ulceration; Candida gives white plaques, usually in immunosuppressed patients.

pharm-tox:hemerx.q: Hemolysis in G6PD deficiency can be triggered by:
pharm-tox:hemerx.e: Also sulfonamides and nitrofurantoin. Oxidant stress; Heinz bodies and bite cells.

pharm-tox:hemerx.q: Which drug causes megaloblastic anemia by interfering with folate?
pharm-tox:hemerx.e: Also trimethoprim, phenytoin; hydroxyurea and 5-FU impair DNA synthesis.

pharm-tox:hemerx.q: A 28-year-old Thai man is given primaquine to prevent relapse of P. vivax malaria. Three days later he has dark urine and jaundice; Hb is 8.2 g/dL and the smear shows bite cells. A supravital stain of his blood would most likely show:
pharm-tox:hemerx.e: Oxidant drugs in G6PD deficiency precipitate denatured hemoglobin (Heinz bodies), which splenic macrophages remove to make bite cells; Howell–Jolly bodies indicate asplenia.

pharm-tox:mskrx.q: Gingival hyperplasia is a side effect of:

pharm-tox:mskrx.e: Risk higher with age and glucocorticoids.

pharm-tox:mskrx.q: A 72-year-old man taking prednisone for COPD is treated for community-acquired pneumonia with an oral antibiotic. Five days later he feels a pop at the back of his ankle while climbing stairs and cannot stand on tiptoe. Which antibiotic was he most likely given?
pharm-tox:mskrx.e: Fluoroquinolones cause tendinopathy and Achilles rupture, especially in older patients on glucocorticoids; macrolides do not.

pharm-tox:neurorx.q: Tinnitus, headache and vertigo (cinchonism) are caused by:
Which drug lowers the seizure threshold?

A 24-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa is started on an oral medication to help her quit smoking. Two weeks later she has a generalized tonic–clonic seizure; she has no prior seizure history. Which drug was most likely prescribed?
pharm-tox:neurorx.e: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in bulimia and anorexia; varenicline is not associated with seizures in this way.

pharm-tox:renalrx.q: Drug-induced lupus is classically caused by:
pharm-tox:renalrx.e: Anti-histone antibodies; renal involvement is uncommon.

pharm-tox:renalrx.q: A 60-year-old man taking hydralazine for hypertension for a year develops arthralgia, a facial rash and pleuritic chest pain. Urinalysis and creatinine are normal. Which antibody is most likely positive?
pharm-tox:renalrx.e: Drug-induced lupus (hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid) is marked by anti-histone antibodies and spares the kidneys; anti-dsDNA suggests idiopathic SLE.

pharm-tox:multirx.q: A disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol occurs with:
Which drug combination raises ototoxicity risk most?
pharm-tox:multirx.e: Both are ototoxic; cisplatin and vancomycin are others.

pharm-tox:multirx.q: A 40-year-old woman being treated for bacterial vaginosis drinks two glasses of wine at a party. Within 20 minutes she has facial flushing, throbbing headache, nausea and palpitations. The mechanism of this reaction is:
o: Blockade of MAO in the gut wall
Release of histamine from mast cells
pharm-tox:multirx.e: Metronidazole causes a disulfiram-like reaction by blocking aldehyde dehydrogenase, so acetaldehyde accumulates; blocking alcohol dehydrogenase would prevent acetaldehyde formation.

pharm-tox:cyp.q: A woman on oral contraceptives starts rifampin. Expected effect:
pharm-tox:cyp.e: Rifampin induces CYP3A4; use backup contraception.

pharm-tox:cyp.q: Which drug inhibits CYP450 and can raise warfarin levels?

A 65-year-old man has a stable INR of 2.5 on warfarin. He is treated with trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection, and 5 days later has gum bleeding with INR 6.1. The main mechanism of this interaction is:
o: Increased gut absorption of vitamin K
pharm-tox:cyp.e: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9, which clears the more potent S-warfarin; an inducer would lower the INR instead.

pharm-tox:sulfa.q: A patient with sulfa allergy needs a loop diuretic. Which lacks a sulfonamide group?
Which of these is a sulfa drug?
pharm-tox:sulfa.e: Also sulfasalazine, sulfonylureas, probenecid, thiazides, acetazolamide.

pharm-tox:sulfa.q: A 48-year-old woman with a history of hives after trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole develops a similar urticarial rash a week after starting a new drug for ulcerative colitis. Which drug was most likely started?
pharm-tox:sulfa.e: Sulfasalazine is split into 5-ASA and sulfapyridine, a sulfonamide; mesalamine is 5-ASA alone without the sulfa moiety.

pharm-tox:names.q: A drug ending in -gliflozin is a:
The suffix -zumab means a monoclonal antibody that is:
A 54-year-old man with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 8.4%) on metformin is started on empagliflozin. Two months later he has a genital fungal infection. The new drug acts by:
o: Blocking glucose reabsorption in proximal tubule
Closing K-ATP channels on pancreatic β cells
pharm-tox:names.e: -gliflozins inhibit SGLT2, causing glucosuria and genital mycotic infections; -gliptins inhibit DPP-4 to prolong incretins.

pharm-tox:terato.q: Which antihypertensive class is contraindicated in pregnancy?
pharm-tox:terato.e: Fetal renal damage and oligohydramnios. Labetalol, methyldopa and nifedipine are used in pregnancy.

pharm-tox:terato.q: Ebstein anomaly is associated with fetal exposure to:

A woman with bipolar disorder took a mood stabilizer throughout the first trimester. Prenatal testing showed elevated maternal serum AFP, and her newborn has a lumbosacral myelomeningocele. Which drug did she most likely take?
pharm-tox:terato.e: Valproate inhibits folate-related pathways and causes neural tube defects; lithium is linked to Ebstein anomaly.

pharm-tox:pgx.q: Before starting carbamazepine in a Thai patient, test for:

A 40-year-old Thai man with recurrent gout starts a urate-lowering drug. Four weeks later he has fever, a widespread rash, eosinophilia and elevated transaminases. Which genetic test could have identified his risk before treatment?
pharm-tox:pgx.e: HLA-B*58:01 predicts severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN, DRESS) to allopurinol, common in Thai and Han Chinese; B*15:02 is for carbamazepine.

pharm-tox:antidote.q: A patient with acetaminophen overdose is given N-acetylcysteine. Its mechanism is:
pharm-tox:antidote.e: Glutathione conjugates the toxic metabolite NAPQI; NAC restores the depleted store. Decide treatment from the level on the nomogram, not from symptoms — early poisoning is silent.

pharm-tox:antidote.q: Which antidote carries a risk of precipitating seizures?
pharm-tox:antidote.e: In chronic benzodiazepine users or TCA co-ingestion, abrupt GABA-A reversal can unmask seizures.

pharm-tox:antidote.q: A 23-year-old man is brought in drowsy 3 hours after taking a large dose of amitriptyline. BP 88/54, HR 124, and the ECG shows a QRS of 140 ms with a tall terminal R wave in aVR. Which treatment addresses the finding that most threatens his life?
pharm-tox:antidote.e: TCAs block fast cardiac Na+ channels, widening the QRS and causing arrhythmia. Hypertonic NaHCO3 provides a sodium load and alkalemia that stabilize the membrane. Physostigmine is for pure antimuscarinic poisoning and is dangerous here.

pharm-tox:antidote2.q: In organophosphate poisoning, atropine is given before pralidoxime because atropine:
o: Blocks nicotinic receptors at the junction
Prevents aging of the bound enzyme
pharm-tox:antidote2.e: Atropine treats bronchorrhea, bronchospasm and bradycardia. Pralidoxime reactivates the enzyme and must be given before aging.

pharm-tox:antidote2.q: Which poisoning is treated with fomepizole?
pharm-tox:antidote2.e: Fomepizole inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing formation of the toxic metabolites. It is preferred to ethanol; dialysis is added in severe cases.

pharm-tox:antidote2.q: A 4-year-old Thai boy is treated for methemoglobinemia with methylene blue, but his cyanosis worsens and his hemoglobin falls from 11 to 7 g/dL with bite cells on the smear. Which underlying condition best explains this?
pharm-tox:antidote2.e: Methylene blue needs NADPH from the HMP shunt to work, so in G6PD deficiency it is both ineffective and an oxidant stress that causes hemolysis. G6PD deficiency is common in Thailand, so it must be considered before giving it.

title.en: Boss case: Spells of pounding headache

boss.case: A 42-year-old woman has episodes of pounding headache, palpitations and sweating. BP during a spell is 210/120 mm Hg. Plasma free metanephrines are high, and CT shows a 4-cm adrenal mass. Surgery is planned.

qs.q: Why must a β-blocker not be given first?
qs.e: β₂ vasodilation is lost. This can precipitate a hypertensive crisis.

qs.q: Phenoxybenzamine's blockade cannot be overcome by more agonist because it is:
o: A partial agonist at α receptors
An inverse agonist at α receptors
qs.e: Shifts the dose–response curve down. Irreversible blockade ↓ efficacy (Emax).

qs.q: Epinephrine at high doses mainly acts on:

title.th: หนังตาตกตอนเย็น

stem.th: หญิง 32 ปี หนังตาตก เห็นภาพซ้อน เป็นมากตอนเย็นและหลังใช้แรง
stem.en: A 32-year-old woman has ptosis and diplopia that worsen in the evening and after exertion.

steps.e: AChE inhibitor ↑ ACh at the NMJ.

steps.q: Muscarinic side effects of pyridostigmine (diarrhea, cramps) are reduced with:

steps.e: Fewer functional receptors; MG patients are resistant to succinylcholine.

info.th: ต้องผ่าตัด thymectomy ใช้ยาหย่อนกล้ามเนื้อ

steps.q: Which antibiotic class may worsen myasthenia?
steps.e: Impair neuromuscular transmission; fluoroquinolones and macrolides can too.

title.th: ยาหลายตัวกับวัณโรค
title.en: Many pills and a TB diagnosis

stem.th: หญิง 30 ปี ได้รับการวินิจฉัยวัณโรคปอด กินยาคุมกำเนิดชนิดรวม และ warfarin จากลิ้นหัวใจเทียม
stem.en: A 30-year-old woman with newly diagnosed pulmonary TB takes a combined oral contraceptive and warfarin for a mechanical valve.

steps.q: Rifampin will affect her other drugs because it:
Expected change in her INR after starting rifampin:
o: INR rises — warfarin dose must fall
INR falls — warfarin dose must rise
INR becomes too erratic to measure
No change — keep the same warfarin dose
No change; the pill stays reliable
Use a non-hormonal or backup method
steps.e: Induction lowers estrogen and progestin levels.
